$comment: Derived from the VMware Cloud Foundation Operations OpenAPI document. Do not hand-edit: regenerate from the pinned specification revision recorded in docs/official_sources.json.

authorization.$comment: The securityScheme above is copied verbatim from the specification, which declares an apiKey carried in the Authorization header but does not name the value prefix. 'OpsToken ' is what VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops 13.5.0 puts on the wire, so it is what the mock accepts and the verifier asserts.

acquireToken.calledBy: Connect-VcfOpsServer, while establishing the connection the caller hands to the module.

getResources.calledBy: The module. This is the only operation the module itself issues.
getResources.$comment: Every parameter is optional. They are listed below in the order the specification declares them, which is the order VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops emits them in the query string. Parameters the caller did not supply are absent from the query string entirely.

parameters.name: recentlyAdded
parameters.$comment: Seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. There is no default: 0 is a real value meaning 'since the epoch', not 'unset'.

omitUnsetOptionalParameters.rule: A parameter the caller did not supply must not appear in the query string in any form.
notAcceptable: resourceKind= (empty value for an array parameter)
omitUnsetOptionalParameters.$comment: The specification gives none of these parameters a default other than page and pageSize, so a value on the wire is a filter the server will apply. An empty or zero-valued filter is a different query from no filter at all.

arrayParameters.rule: An array parameter is repeated once per value, in the order the caller supplied them: resourceKind=HostSystem&resourceKind=VirtualMachine.

parameterOrder.rule: Query parameters appear in the order the specification declares them, with page and pageSize last.

percentEncoding.rule: Values are percent-encoded; '|' is sent as %7C.

pagination.$comment: page is a page ordinal, not a row offset. The second page of a pageSize=5 enumeration is page=1, not page=5.

terminationSignal.rule: The collection is exhausted when the response carries no link whose rel is NEXT. Fetch pages until that link is absent, and stop there.

unreliableSignals.pageInfo.totalCount: Advisory. It is the count the server had when it computed the page and the inventory is live, so it may be smaller or larger than the number of resources actually returned. It must not be used to decide when to stop.
unreliableSignals.resourceList.length: A page may carry fewer entries than pageSize and still not be the last page: the server applies some filters after it has cut the page. A short page must not be read as the end of the collection.

pagination.duplicatesAcrossPages: Because pages are computed independently against a live inventory, one resource may appear on more than one page. A resource identifier must appear at most once in the result.

ordering.rule: Ascending by resourceKey.name, ties broken ascending by identifier.
ordering.$comment: Ordinal means System.StringComparison.Ordinal: compare by code unit. The server returns resources in no particular order and the API declares no sort, so the order has to be imposed by the client. It has to be ordinal rather than culture-aware so that the same inventory produces the same output on every host: PowerShell's default comparison follows the current culture, which orders 'vsan-cluster-A' against 'vsan-cluster-a', and 'ds-local-01' against 'ds_local-01', differently than code-unit order does.
